question: How many cards must a Commander deck have?
key_facts: Exactly 100 cards.
The commander counts toward the 100.

question: Can I run more than one copy of a card in Commander?
key_facts: No: each card must have a different English name, so one copy of each.
Basic lands are the exception.

question: Which cards can go in my deck, given my commander's colors?
key_facts: A card can be included only if every color in its color identity is in the commander's color identity.

question: Does reminder text count toward a card's color identity?
key_facts: No: reminder text is ignored when determining color identity.

question: Does the back face of a double-faced card count for color identity?
key_facts: Yes: the back face is included in the card's color identity.

question: What life total do players start with in Commander?
key_facts: 40 life.

question: How much more does my commander cost each time I recast it from the command zone?
key_facts: {2} more for each previous time it was cast from the command zone that game.

question: What happens when my commander would die or be exiled?
key_facts: Its owner may put it into the command zone (it's optional).

question: Can my commander go to the command zone instead of my hand or library?
key_facts: Yes: if it would go to its owner's hand or library from anywhere, its owner may put it into the command zone instead (it's optional).

question: How much commander damage makes a player lose?
key_facts: 21 or more combat damage from the same commander over the game.
That player loses the game.

question: Can a Vehicle be my commander?
key_facts: Yes: a legendary Vehicle card can be a commander.

question: A planeswalker says it can be your commander. Is that allowed?
key_facts: Yes: a card whose text says it can be your commander may be your commander.

question: Where does my commander start the game?
key_facts: In the command zone, face up.

question: Can I include a land with a basic land type that makes a color outside my commander's identity?
key_facts: No: a card with a basic land type can be included only if each color of mana it could produce is in the commander's color identity.

question: How do partner commanders work?
key_facts: A partner ability lets you have two legendary cards as your commander instead of one.
Each kind of partner ability has its own requirements for the pair.

question: Is the first mulligan free in a multiplayer game?
key_facts: Yes: in a multiplayer game the first mulligan doesn't count toward the cards put on the bottom of the library.

question: What does deathtouch do?
key_facts: Any nonzero damage from a source with deathtouch destroys a creature.

question: How does a creature with trample assign its combat damage?
key_facts: It must assign lethal damage to all its blockers before it can assign any to the player, planeswalker or battle it's attacking.
Damage beyond that can be assigned to the player, planeswalker or battle.

question: How does lifelink work?
key_facts: Damage dealt by a source with lifelink makes its controller gain that much life.

question: What does hexproof mean?
key_facts: It can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control.

question: Can an indestructible creature be destroyed by damage?
key_facts: No: an indestructible permanent isn't destroyed by lethal damage.

question: When can I cast a spell with flash?
key_facts: Any time you could cast an instant.

question: What does ward do when my creature is targeted?
key_facts: When it becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, that spell or ability is countered unless its controller pays the ward cost.

question: How does cascade work?
key_facts: When you cast the spell, you exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card whose mana value is less than the cascading spell's mana value.
You may cast that card without paying its mana cost.
The other exiled cards go on the bottom of your library in a random order.

question: How does storm copy a spell?
key_facts: When you cast the spell, you copy it for each other spell cast before it that turn.
You may choose new targets for the copies.

question: How does flashback let me cast a card from my graveyard?
key_facts: You may cast it from your graveyard by paying its flashback cost.
If cast with flashback, it's exiled when it leaves the stack.

question: What does it mean to mill cards?
key_facts: You put that many cards from the top of your library into your graveyard.

question: What happens to a permanent when it phases out?
key_facts: While phased out it's treated as though it doesn't exist.
It phases back in during its controller's next untap step.

question: How does ninjutsu work?
key_facts: From your hand, you pay its cost, reveal it, and return an unblocked attacking creature you control to its owner's hand.
The card is put onto the battlefield tapped and attacking.

question: What does proliferate do?
key_facts: Choose any number of permanents and/or players that have counters.
Each gets one more counter of each kind it already has.

question: How does double strike deal damage in combat?
key_facts: It deals combat damage twice: in the first-strike combat damage step and again in the regular combat damage step.

question: What happens if I control two legendary permanents with the same name?
key_facts: You choose one, and the rest are put into their owners' graveyards (the legend rule).

question: What happens to a creature with 0 toughness?
key_facts: It's put into its owner's graveyard.

question: What happens if I have to draw from an empty library?
key_facts: You lose the game.

question: When does a player lose the game for having no life?
key_facts: When their life total is 0 or less.

question: Why can't my creature use a tap ability the turn it enters?
key_facts: A creature's abilities with the tap or untap symbol in their cost can't be activated unless it's been under your control continuously since your most recent turn began (summoning sickness).

question: What happens to a token that leaves the battlefield?
key_facts: It ceases to exist once it's in a zone other than the battlefield.

question: What happens to a spell that gets countered?
key_facts: It's removed from the stack without resolving, so none of its effects happen.
It's put into its owner's graveyard.

question: What is the mana value of a card with X in its cost?
key_facts: X is treated as 0 everywhere except on the stack.
On the stack, X is the number chosen for it.

question: How many lands can I play each turn?
key_facts: One land per turn, normally; effects can allow more.

question: What is the maximum hand size, and when do I discard down to it?
key_facts: Seven cards, normally.
You discard down to it during your cleanup step.

question: Which spell on the stack resolves first?
key_facts: The last one added (the top of the stack) resolves first, once all players pass in succession.

question: How do extra turns work?
key_facts: An extra turn is taken directly after the specified turn.
With several extra turns, the most recently created one is taken first.

question: What is a Treasure token?
key_facts: A colorless Treasure artifact token.
{T}, sacrifice it: add one mana of any color.

question: What does it mean to sacrifice a permanent?
key_facts: Its controller moves it from the battlefield directly to its owner's graveyard.
It isn't destroyed, so regeneration can't save it.

question: Is it OK to use proxies in a casual Commander game?
notes: Proxy policy is set by Wizards' tournament documents and playgroups, not the Comprehensive Rules.

question: Which cards are currently banned in Commander?
notes: The banned list is published separately, not in the Comprehensive Rules.

question: Is Sol Ring worth putting in my deck?
notes: Card strength is a matter of opinion, not rules.

question: Which power bracket is my Commander deck in?
notes: The Commander brackets are a separate Wizards guide, not part of the Comprehensive Rules.

question: How long is a round at a Magic tournament?
notes: Round length is in the Magic Tournament Rules, not the Comprehensive Rules.

question: What's the penalty for drawing an extra card at a Competitive event?
notes: Penalties are in the Infraction Procedure Guide, not the Comprehensive Rules.

Who won the most recent Magic World Championship?
notes: Event results aren't in the rules.

question: When is the next Commander banned list update?
notes: Announcement dates aren't in the rules.

question: Can I use sleeves of different colors in a tournament?
notes: Sleeve requirements are in the Magic Tournament Rules, not the Comprehensive Rules.
